newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish treasury sets privatisation outline to 2000.
newsitem.headline: Polish treasury sets privatisation outline to 2000.

text.p: The Polish Treasury Ministry prepared privatisation guidelines until the year 2000, which included allocating revenues to reforming the social security system and to beef up the budget.
"According to the guidelines all sectors apart from natural resources and infrastructure can be privatised," Minister Miroslaw Pietrewicz told a news conference on Wednesday.
"Privatisation should be used to meet social and economic needs," Pietrewicz added. @

Revenues from the privatisation of state-owned property would be used to finance the pension reform, meet claims of owner of property confiscated under communism, strengthen the budget and pay off public debt, he said.
Pietrewicz declined to give the value of revenues from privatisations in future years, but said the value of all state-owned firms was roughly 145 billion zlotys.
"According to our estimates, we will have to earmark some 45 billion zlotys for the social insurance reform, and another 8-10 billion zlotys for reprivatisation," Pietrewicz said. @
He said this year the revenues from direct sales of companies to investors or flotations were expected to reach 4.5 billion zlotys compared to 1.85 billion in 1996.
